judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Thumbnail of the first related-news card (A youth-led vision for social media and mental health), lazy-loaded from Untitled-design-34.png. The crop and the screenshot show a photo of young people in hoodies; the alt describes the IAYMH 2026 logo with its text, which the picture does not contain. The theme reuses the current post's featured-image alt on every related card. I looked for a reason it could pass: the image is not decorative-only with a null alt, and even if it were meant to be ignored a non-null misleading alt fails (F39); an alt that describes another image does not serve the equivalent purpose (1.1.1). The live HTML fetched on 2026-11-21 carries the same markup (same alt, title and data-lazy-src for all three related-news thumbnails), and the screenshot shows the same pictures as the crops, so the capture does not differ. The claim names the defect.

Live HTML matches the capture (same markup, no aria). The claim names the failure.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: Instagram icon, the only content of a footer link to instagram.com/jigsaw_ymh, under the h3 'Social Media'. Its alt (and title) is 'ri_instagram-line', the Remix Icon file name. The claim says it does not say where the link leads, but the string contains 'instagram', which names the destination site in the same way the neighbouring 'Facebook' alt does; read under 'Social Media' users can tell it opens Jigsaw's Instagram. Against that, it is a file name with noise ('ri_', '-line'), which F30 lists as a text alternative that is not an alternative. I lean towards it meeting H30's purpose test, but competent auditors would split on a file name that happens to contain the destination's name. Live HTML matches the capture (no aria-label on the link). The snapshot's link name, an HTML string from the noscript fallback, is a collector artefact that does not affect the image's alt.
